about: Synthetic data. More everyday capsules from Marina (fictional). Small details are planted early and resolved years later, to test whether a model really reads the whole life.

capsules.text: Moved into the república on Rua XV today. Four girls, one bathroom, a fridge with names on every yogurt. My room smells like old wood. I put the drawing of the sea Vó Lúcia framed for me above the bed. Future me: is it still above your bed?

Tio Beto taught me three chords on his old violão at Sunday lunch. I promised him I'd learn to play 'Asa Branca' all the way through by the next Festa Junina. He laughed and said he's heard that promise from every cousin. Prove him wrong, Marina.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. There's an old man who carries a green parrot on his shoulder every single day. The parrot says 'bom dia, motorista'. Nobody on the bus reacts anymore except me. I drew them both in the margin of my Álgebra notebook.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream since I was a kid: I'm standing at the edge, the water is warm, I want to go in and I can't, my feet won't move. I wake up with my calves tight. Five years from now, I hope the dream changed.
Bia's 18th birthday. We wrote our names on the wall of the bar in São Francisco with a marker. If the wall's been painted over by the time you read this, that's fine. We were there.
Money check: R$ 340 left for the month and it's the 28th. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this so in two years I can laugh at it. Or cry. Depends.
Mom called to ask if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. I have a sketchbook under the mattress like it's something illegal.
Summer in Matinhos. Bia tried to teach me to float. I lasted four seconds before panicking. A kid of maybe six floated next to me the whole time, out of pure spite I think.

First date with Rafa. Pastel de feira and a walk in the Passeio Público. He talked about São Paulo the entire time, the jobs, the buildings, the noise, like it's a person he's in love with. I talked about the sea. We both pretended not to notice.

Vó Lúcia told me the story of Coronel today, the farm dog in Irati who walked her to school for nine years and waited at the gate. When he died, her father buried him under the jabuticabeira. She cried telling it, sixty years later. I want to draw this one day.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I played 'Asa Branca' until the second verse and then forgot everything. Tio Beto clapped anyway and said 'one more year'. One more year.
The parrot man wasn't on the bus for a week and I was genuinely worried. Today he was back with a bandage on his hand. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I'm counting it.

Ate a lemon at the república and, for no reason, planted three seeds in a yogurt cup with 'MARINA' written on it (thanks, fridge rules). If even one sprouts I'm keeping it forever. Ten years, future me. Do you still have a lemon tree?
One of the lemon seeds sprouted! Two tiny leaves. The girls named it Limonada. It lives on the windowsill next to my sketchbook, which no longer hides under the mattress.

The bus comics have a name now: 'Interbairros'. The most popular character is 'Seu Ivo e o Papagaio', based on the parrot man (I don't know his real name, I invented Ivo). People ask what the parrot's name is. I said Juca.
Rafa and I watched the Olympics closing ceremony at his parents' house. His mom asked when we're getting married. He said 'when she agrees to São Paulo'. Everyone laughed. I didn't.

Mom saw the Interbairros page. She didn't say anything for two days. Then she sent me a screenshot of one strip with the message 'this old man looks like your grandfather'. It's the closest thing to a compliment I've ever had from her about drawing.
Failed the driving test. Stalled the car on the hill in front of the Detran examiner. He wrote something and didn't look at me. Second try in March.
Failed the driving test again. Same hill. I'm convinced the hill is personal. I'm taking a break from cars.

Dia dos Namorados. Rafa, I'm writing this one to you but I don't know if I'll ever let it arrive. You got the offer in São Paulo. You're going. I'm proud of you and I'm so tired of pretending I want to follow.
Limonada survived a frost on the windowsill. I brought her inside wrapped in my scarf. Eight leaves. She's taller than the yogurt cup now, moved her to a real pot.
At the factory the senior engineer, Cláudio, saw me sketching a motor during lunch and asked if I could draw the assembly diagrams for the new line. Turns out drawing is useful. Who knew. (Mom.)
Same sea dream, but this time I put one foot in. Probably because of the breakup. The therapist I don't have yet would have something to say about that.
Festa Junina. Didn't even try 'Asa Branca'. Tio Beto didn't ask. That's worse than him asking.

Money check: first salary. R$ 3.800. I paid Mom back the R$ 600 from the dentist in 2015 and she refused, so I bought her a printer. She uses it to print my comics. She hasn't said that, Bia's mom told me.
Opened the breakup capsule from last year. It was right. I'm OK. Better than OK, I think: I spent the weekend drawing and didn't once check his Instagram. (Twice.)
PASSED THE DRIVING TEST. Different examiner, different hill. I drove to Vó Lúcia's to show her the license and she made me drive her to the bakery and back three times.

Seu Ivo (the parrot man) hasn't been on the bus for a month. The driver said he moved in with his daughter in Ponta Grossa. I drew a final strip: Juca the parrot saying 'tchau, motorista'. 2.000 likes. I cried a bit at the bus stop.
Visited Bia in Floripa for the first time. The spare room really faces the sea. I stood at the window for twenty minutes. She took a photo of my back and captioned it 'finally'.

New Year at Vó Lúcia's this time, she didn't want to travel to the beach. She stayed awake until midnight just to prove she could. Her hands were cold when she held mine. Write it down: her hands were cold and she held on.

Called Vó, she told me about the jabuticabeira at the farm and how Coronel is buried under it. She's told me this story five times. I wrote down every version. They're slightly different each time; Coronel gets braver.
Limonada is four years old, a meter tall, and has never given a single lemon. Bia says it's because she's a 'decorative lemon'. I refuse.

First Christmas without Vó. Mom made the bolo de fubá and it was wrong, too dry, and nobody said anything. Then Mom said it herself and we all laughed and then cried. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' on the violão without being asked. I didn't sing.
Mom asked to see the drawings of Vó's stories. I showed her the 14 I have. She went quiet and said 'you got her hands right'. I didn't know I had.
Swimming lesson #20. I can float now. Dona Cida says floating is about trust, not technique. I said that's very poetic for 7am. She splashed me.
The sea dream changed. I went in. The water was warm and someone was swimming next to me but I couldn't see who. Woke up and wasn't sad.
Cláudio from the factory retired. At the party he said 'you were the only engineer who drew better than the CAD'. I'm putting it on my tombstone.
Money check: I have six months of savings for the first time. That's my courage fund. It has a name in the bank app: 'MAR'.
First month at the solar startup. My manager, Thaís, asked for 'something less technical' on a diagram and I drew a little sun with sunglasses. It's now in the investor deck.
Festa Junina. Tio Beto handed me the violão without a word. I played 'Asa Branca' until the end. ALL of it. Nine years late. He said 'I told you, one more year' as if it had been one.
Lisbon, day 12. In a tiny shop in Alfama I found a postcard of a man with a parrot on his shoulder, from the 1950s. Bought it for R$ 2 worth of euros. It's on my laptop now.
Mom asked if Lisbon would be 'forever'. I said I don't know. She said 'your grandmother always said you were menina do mar, not menina de Curitiba'. I didn't know Vó said that to her too.

Decision: Florianópolis, not Lisbon. Closer to Mom, Bia already there, and the sea is the same ocean, technically. Limonada comes with me in the back seat of the car, which I can drive, which is still a miracle.
Limonada lives on Bia's balcony now, facing the sea. Eight years old. She got her first flowers. Small, white, smell incredible. No lemons yet but flowers count.
Swam in the sea alone for the first time, Praia Mole, early morning. Not far. Far enough. Nobody watching. That's the part 18-year-old me wouldn't believe.
Bia and Júlia got engaged on the balcony, next to Limonada. I was hiding in my room pretending to work so they'd have the moment. I heard the scream through the wall. Wedding in 2026.

At a comics fair in Curitiba a woman came to my table holding an old printed 'Interbairros' strip. Seu Ivo e o Papagaio. She said 'this is my grandfather, Valdir. The parrot was Juca'. I had invented both names. Only one was wrong. He died last year, at 91. She said he had the strip on his fridge.
Money check: half my income comes from illustration now. Thaís lets me work four days a week. The 'MAR' savings fund turned into the 'book' fund.
New Year on the balcony. Mom, Bia, Júlia, me, and Limonada with a tiny green ball in her branches. Could be a lemon. Could be my imagination. Not jinxing it.

The yogurt-cup capsule from 2016 arrived today. 'Do you still have a lemon tree?' Yes. Limonada is ten. And this morning I picked her first lemon. It is small and ugly and the most beautiful thing I own.

Bia and Júlia's wedding in the garden. I gave the speech and drew the invitations. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' and handed me the violão halfway through. I finished it. Bia cried at the wrong part, as usual.

Same sea dream, first time in years. I was already swimming. I turned around and the person swimming next to me was Vó Lúcia, young, laughing like stairs. I woke up and drew it before it faded. It's the last page of the book.
